schema.frame: Moon mean-Earth/polar-axis (ME/PA) body-fixed frame; latitude planetocentric (Moon treated as sphere R=1737.4 km, as in JPL Horizons); longitude east-positive in -180..180. Altitude not specified (use 0 over the 1737.4 km sphere unless a DEM is added).
schema.verified_meaning: true = coordinates copied from a retrieved primary source (NSSDCA/LROC/IAU Gazetteer). It does NOT mean they are NASA landing-region centres: see coordinate_basis.

coordinate_basis_values.point: published point coordinate of the site
coordinate_basis_values.feature_centre: IAU Gazetteer centre of the named feature; the NASA Artemis III region is on/near it but its centre is not published by NASA

source.note: Wagner et al. 2017 (Icarus 283, 92-103) via NSSDCA, page updated 2017-03-06; planetocentric Mean Earth/Polar Axis, DE421. Matches frontend/src/viewports/bodies/registry.ts. IAU Gazetteer Statio Tranquillitatis (feature 5684) rounds to 0.67, 23.47.
Same source and frame as Apollo 11. Matches frontend registry.ts.

sites.name: Malapert Massif (Artemis III candidate region; Mons Malapert)

source.note: IAU Gazetteer centre of Mons Malapert (feature 16338), not a NASA region centre. NASA lists the region by name only (no coordinates). LROC page https://lroc.im-ldi.com/images/1294 (2023-03-14) says '(86S, 0E)' is the heart of the Artemis 3 region, consistent within ~2 deg of longitude. Gazetteer coordinate-system field: 'Planetographic, +East, -180-180'.
IAU Gazetteer centre of Haworth crater (51.42 km diameter), feature 14502. NASA names the region but publishes no coordinates; actual landing sites would be on/near the rim, offset from this centre.

IAU Gazetteer centre of Mons Mouton (feature 16070, 130 km extent, so region offset may be tens of km). LROC https://lroc.im-ldi.com/images/1401 (2025-02-26) gives IM-2 intended landing site -84.78, 29.13E, stated to be in the central portion of an Artemis III candidate region.

sites.name: Nobile Rim 1/2 (Artemis III candidate regions; Nobile crater)

source.note: IAU Gazetteer centre of Nobile crater (79.27 km diameter), feature 4321. Nobile Rim 1 and 2 are on the rim, so true region centres are up to ~40 km from this point; NASA gives no coordinates.

sites.name: de Gerlache (Artemis III candidate 'de Gerlache Rim 2'; crater)

source.note: IAU Gazetteer centre of de Gerlache crater (32.71 km), feature 1439. NASA names region 'de Gerlache Rim 2' only; rim offset up to ~16 km from centre.

IAU Gazetteer centre of Shackleton crater (feature 5450). 'Peak near Shackleton' was in NASA's 2022 list of 13 but not in the 2024 list of nine. Included as a near-pole extreme-geometry case. At |lat|>89.6 deg longitude is nearly degenerate.
